nodes.title: Test shot (<Picture 1-5> face, <Picture 6-9> body = the outfit)
Read me
widgets_values:
## 8. Photo to RefCap in one queue
Makes RefCaps from a single photo: H3 renders two 180-degree studio orbits of the person, one round each side, **H3 RefCap Orbit Views** picks frames labelled with the angle they were seen from, and two face RefCaps are saved in `models/refcaps/`; the body section adds a full-body RefCap. A short test clip renders at the end. One queue runs it all.

**Steps**
1. Load the photo in **Your photo**: one person, face clearly visible.
2. Edit `subject_definitions` in **both** orbit prompts if the back of the head matters: age, hair, and anything seen only from behind (a braid, hair clip, hood). H3 has to invent the back, so the prompt is all it has.
3. Set the three `name`s and queue. The two orbits take about 75 s each at 768x768 on a 12 GB card, the test about 85 s, the body section about 3 minutes; check the orbit videos really turn all the way round. The H3 shots run back to back, which on a 12 GB card needs ComfyUI started with `--vram-headroom 0.75`; without it the second shot fails at once with CUDA out of memory.
4. Refresh the browser so the new files appear in the RefCap lists.

**What you get**
- **`my_character_front`**: the views nearest 0, +-20 and +-45 degrees, the best set for faces. Use it in workflow 5 with `select` = `all`.
- **`my_character_turnaround`**: 24 views every 15 degrees round the head. Use it in workflow 5 with `select` = `nearest` and the angles your shot shows, for shots of the side or back of the head.
- **Test render**: a full-body walk from the front 5 and the body views at 0, +-90 and 180 degrees, fed to the native reference node. It runs at `ref_image_size` = `match`, because nine pictures at `max` run out of memory on 12 GB right after the renders, so it shows a little less detail than Replay of the RefCaps, which uses their stored `max` size. Its prompt names the body pictures as the clothing source, so it previews identity and outfit together. Mute the *Test render* group (select it, Ctrl+M) to skip it.

**Body section** (bottom group): a full-body RefCap for outfits.
- **The switch** picks the full-body photo. On (default): H3 renders a short full-body clip from your head shot and takes its last frame (saved as `h3_refcap/body_photo`). **Describe the outfit in *Generate a full-body photo*.** Off: load your own head-to-toe photo in **Full-body photo**; only the chosen branch runs.
- Two full-body orbits at 576x1024 see the head shot as `<Picture 1>` and the body photo as `<Picture 2>`, so both copy the same outfit, and **`my_character_body`** gets views near 0, +-45, +-90 and 180 degrees.
- The face is small in a full-body frame, so insightface loses it early and the body views' angles are rough (labelled 46 and 92, they looked closer to 65 and 130 in the first test).
- Combine face and body per shot with workflow 7: *Select* each file, or *Bake* them into one file. A baked file and the two files selected together give the same conditioning, bit for bit. A shot takes at most 9 pictures, e.g. 5 face + 4 body.
- **When you combine them, name the body pictures as the clothing source:** `<Subject 1> is the woman in <Picture 1>, ... and <Picture 9>, wearing exactly what she wears in <Picture 6>, <Picture 7>, <Picture 8> and <Picture 9>.` In the first test, face + body without that line lost the outfit in 4 of 4 clips (the bare-shouldered head shots won); with it, the outfit came through in 4 of 4, and identity was as good as or better than face views alone. Body views alone keep the outfit but weaken the face.
- It adds about 3 minutes per run.

**H3 RefCap Orbit Views**
- H3's orbits ease in, so frame position is a poor guide to the angle. With `measure` = `faces`, insightface measures each frame's head yaw up to 75 degrees, and the rest is interpolated to 180 at the last frame (it needs the `insightface` package and `models/insightface/models/buffalo_l`). `steady` assumes a steady turn.
- `yaws` picks the angles (negative = the left orbit). Empty takes every 15 degrees.
- The picked frames are rounded to 8 bits, as saved frames would be, so the build stores them as PNGs.

**What to expect** (measured on a generated portrait, 45 clips per arm, face similarity): **5 front views 0.639**, 9 views round the head 0.633, the orbit as a clip 0.605, 5 views chosen per shot 0.637. The turnaround is real (7 of 24 views were true back views), but it **doesn't improve identity**: H3's back views are inferred from the same front photo, so they add no information, and they lose slightly where the head is turned furthest (-0.03 past 70 degrees). They even diluted a detail visible from the front (a hair comb: 3/3 front-view clips, 0/3 with the ring). **Real photos from more angles beat it**; with just one photo, capturing that photo directly (workflow 1) is the plain alternative.

**Settings in these workflows** follow ComfyUI's MiniMax H3 reference-to-video template: the ref2va model with its 4-step Lightning LoRA, 4 steps, `res_multistep` + `simple`, 608x352. For the base model, bypass the *Lightning LoRA* node and use 20 steps. The measurements quoted here ran on a community H3 turbo finetune (shift 6/3, 8 steps) on a 12 GB GPU. Raise the size and length for final renders; the reference tokens ride through every step, so more photos and larger captures cost time.

nodes.title: Prompt guide
widgets_values:
## Writing the prompt
H3's reference mode reads a structured prompt. The photos are labelled in order: `<Picture 1>` ... `<Picture N>`, where N is the number of photos in the RefCap.

```
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the woman in <Picture 1>, <Picture 2> and <Picture 3>, a white woman in her mid-twenties with dark brown, wavy, shoulder-length hair.

summary:
[reference generation] <Subject 1> sits at a sunlit cafe table and smiles at the camera.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the woman's facial identity and hairstyle are retained.

detailed_description:
The target video is a realistic, full-color cinematic shot with warm daylight.
[Shot 1] A medium close-up shows <Subject 1>, wearing a navy t-shirt, ...

overall_soundscape:
Gentle street ambience.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A
```

**Tips**
- Describe age, gender and hair, and **say the outfit and action you want**. The photos supply the face; the prompt supplies everything else.
- Don't count on a name. The tests never used one.
- More detail in `detailed_description` (camera, lighting, motion, sound) gives better shots. MiniMax's guide suggests 350-500 words for final renders.
- Official format guide: MiniMax-H3 `docs/VIDEO_PROMPT_WRITING_GUIDE_ref_en.md`.
